mainTopic: The sheet-versus-shutter answer, the praise of רבי אליעזר, his teacher רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and הלל's students, and the new משניות about sitting in the סוכה and who is exempt.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a question from the previous amud. The גמרא explains that a shutter becomes part of the building, but a sheet spread over a סוכה does not, because it is meant to be removed. It then tells how people in the Upper Galilee asked רבי אליעזר thirty questions about סוכה, and he answered only what he had heard from his teachers. When challenged, he described his habits, which he learned from his teacher רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. The גמרא praises רבן יוחנן בן זכאי as the 'smallest' of הלל's eighty students, yet a master of every kind of Torah wisdom. From there it reasons that the greatest student, יונתן בן עוזיאל, was greater still. A new משנה follows, in which בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about someone whose table is in the house, and the משנה then teaches that נשים, עבדים and קטנים are exempt from סוכה. The גמרא looks for the source of the exemption in the word הָאֶזְרָח and raises a contradiction from יום כפור, which רבה answers by calling both rules הלכות. Finally it asks why any source is needed at all, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Shutter vs. sheet: one is permanent, one is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא separates the shutter case from the sheet case. Closing a shutter makes it part of the building. A sheet is not meant to stay, so it is not necessarily forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with the shutter, he cancels its separate status, so it becomes part of the structure. But here, with the sheet, he does not cancel it, so the same rule does not necessarily apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier comparison. The shutter case was stricter because the person made the shutter a fixed part of the building, while the sheet is temporary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is בִּטּוּל: treating an object as a permanent part of the structure. A closed shutter becomes part of the building. A sheet spread against the sun is meant to be taken down, so it is never cancelled into the סוכה, and the proof from the shutter case does not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: He cancels / makes it a permanent part of the structure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying the sheet is definitely permitted. The גמרא only says the shutter case does not prove it forbidden. That is why רבי אליעזר could avoid giving a ruling.

phrases.english: There it is where he negates it,
phrases.notes: The shutter case: closing the window makes the shutter part of the building.

phrases.english: but here, where he does not negate it, no.
phrases.notes: The sheet is meant to be removed, so it is not part of the structure.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם הוּא דִּמְבַטֵּל, אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלָא מְבַטֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the comparison to the shutter case, which appeared on the previous amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The shutter case might prove that spreading a sheet is also forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shutter is cancelled into the building, but the sheet is not, so the comparison fails.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר is asked thirty questions about סוכה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how רבי אליעזר, spending שבת in the Upper Galilee, was asked thirty questions about סוכה. He gave twelve answers from tradition and said he had not heard about eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Once רבי אליעזר stayed in the Upper Galilee. People asked him thirty laws about סוכה. For twelve he said 'I heard,' and for eighteen he said 'I did not hear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related story showing that רבי אליעזר often answered only with what he had received from his teachers. This explains why he avoided the sheet question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story supports the idea that רבי אליעזר's silence on the sheet question was not a hidden prohibition. He simply had no tradition about it. The numbers show that he openly said 'I did not hear' even about many questions.

keyTerms.meaning: I heard (I have a tradition from my teachers)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
An incident with Rabbi Eliezer
who stayed in the Upper Galilee,
and they asked him thirty laws
in the laws of sukkah.
About twelve he said to them: I heard;

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה אָמַר לָהֶם: לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי.
phrases.english: about eighteen he said to them: I did not hear.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related story that explains רבי אליעזר's evasive answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר answered only from received tradition and openly admitted when he had none.

steps.title: A reversed version of the numbers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה reports the story with the numbers reversed: eighteen answered from tradition and twelve not heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי the son of רבי יהודה says it was the opposite: for eighteen he said 'I heard,' and for twelve he said 'I did not hear.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives a different version of the same story, with the numbers swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is only about the numbers. Both versions agree on the main point: רבי אליעזר answered only from tradition and said plainly when he did not know.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
The matters were reversed:
About eighteen he said to them: I heard;

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה אָמַר לָהֶם: לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי.
phrases.english: about twelve he said to them: I did not hear.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, חִילּוּף הַדְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of the numbers in the same story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eighteen were answered from tradition and twelve were not.

steps.title: The people challenge רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The people ask רבי אליעזר whether everything he says comes only from what he heard. Does he never rule on his own?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Are all your words only from what you heard?
steps.whatsHappening: The questioners push רבי אליעזר. They ask why he never uses his own reasoning. This sets up his personal answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grammatically this is a question, but it also has the feel of a gentle challenge. A great scholar should be able to reason things out. His answer will explain that his policy is deliberate.

keyTerms.meaning: From received tradition (literally, 'from the mouth of what was heard')

phrases.english: They said to him: Are all your words nothing
but from what you have heard?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כׇּל דְּבָרֶיךָ אֵינָן אֶלָּא מִפִּי הַשְּׁמוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to his many 'I did not hear' answers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אליעזר ever says anything based on his own reasoning.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר describes his lifelong habits
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says they have forced him to say something he did not hear from his teachers, namely praise of himself. He lists his habits, ending with: he never said anything he had not heard from his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: You have forced me to say something I did not hear from my teachers. In all my days, no one arrived at the בית המדרש before me. I never slept there, not a long sleep and not a nap. I never left anyone behind there when I went out. I never engaged in idle talk. And I never said anything I had not heard from my teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the challenge by describing his total dedication to Torah. His policy of saying only what he heard is part of that dedication.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening line is a clever touch. Talking about himself is itself 'something I did not hear,' so even this answer breaks his usual rule, and only because they pushed him. The list shows that his refusal to make up answers comes from loyalty to his teachers and humility, not from a lack of ability.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבי אליעזר avoided the sheet question. He had no tradition about it, so he would not invent a ruling.

phrases.english: He said to them: You have forced me to say
something that I did not hear from my teachers.

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּמַי לֹא קְדָמַנִי אָדָם בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
phrases.english: In all my days, no person preceded me into the study hall;
and I never slept in the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שֵׁינַת קֶבַע וְלֹא שֵׁינַת עֲרַאי,
phrases.english: neither a settled sleep nor a brief nap;

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הִנַּחְתִּי אָדָם בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וְיָצָאתִי,
phrases.english: and I never left a person in the study hall and went out;
and I never engaged in idle talk;
and I never said anything that I did not hear
from my teacher, ever.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: הִזְקַקְתּוּנִי לוֹמַר דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא שָׁמַעְתִּי מִפִּי רַבּוֹתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, by deliberate policy. As part of his total devotion to Torah, he never says anything he did not receive from his teacher.

steps.title: The habits of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: Because the story mentioned רבי אליעזר's teacher, the גמרא lists the habits of that teacher, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. Many of them match his student's habits.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: In all his days he never engaged in idle talk. He never walked four אמות without Torah and without תפילין. No one arrived at the בית המדרש before him. He never slept there, not a long sleep and not a nap. He never thought about Torah in filthy alleys. He never left anyone behind there when he went out. No one ever found him sitting silently; he was always sitting and learning. No one opened the door for his students except he himself. He never said anything he had not heard from his teacher. He never said 'It is time to leave the בית המדרש,' except on ערב פסח and ערב יום כפור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the student to his teacher. It shows where רבי אליעזר learned his habits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list repeats several of רבי אליעזר's habits and adds more. These include constant Torah and תפילין, respect for Torah by not thinking about it in dirty places, humility in opening the door himself, and never ending the learning session early. The two exceptions have specific reasons. On ערב פסח they had to bring the קרבן פסח, and on ערב יום כפור there is a מצוה to eat.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי:
phrases.english: They said about Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai:
In all his days he never engaged in idle talk;
and he never walked four cubits
without Torah and without tefillin;
and no person preceded him into the study hall;
and he never slept in the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שֵׁינַת קֶבַע וְלֹא שֵׁינַת עֲרַאי,
phrases.english: neither a settled sleep nor a brief nap;
and he never thought about Torah in filthy alleyways;

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הִנִּיחַ אָדָם בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וְיָצָא,
phrases.english: and he never left a person in the study hall and went out;
and no person found him sitting silent,
but only sitting and learning;
and no person opened the door for his students
except he himself;
and he never said anything that he did not hear
from his teacher, ever;
and he never said: The time has come
to get up from the study hall,
except on the eves of Pesach
and the eves of Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mentioning רבי אליעזר's habits leads to describing his teacher's habits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was completely devoted to Torah, humble, and faithful to his teacher's tradition.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר followed his teacher's ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes by noting that רבי אליעזר, the student of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, copied his teacher's conduct.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר, his student, also conducted himself the same way after him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ties the two lists together. רבי אליעזר's habits came straight from his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line explains why the two lists are so similar. Just as רבי אליעזר passed on only his teachers' words, he also copied his teacher's way of life.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר avoided ruling on the sheet question because he never said anything he had not received from his teacher. This was a habit he learned from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, along with total devotion to Torah.

phrases.english: And so Rabbi Eliezer, his student, would
conduct himself after him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר תַּלְמִידוֹ נוֹהֵג אַחֲרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's habits by linking it back to רבי אליעזר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר's conduct, including saying only what he received, was modeled on his teacher רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

steps.title: הלל's eighty students and their levels
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says הלל הזקן had eighty students in three levels. The greatest was יונתן בן עוזיאל and the 'smallest' was רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: הלל הזקן had eighty students. Thirty were worthy for the שכינה to rest on them like משה רבינו. Thirty were worthy for the sun to stand still for them like יהושע בן נון. Twenty were in between. The greatest of them all was יונתן בן עוזיאל, and the smallest of them all was רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The last step ended with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי as רבי אליעזר's teacher. Now the גמרא goes one generation further back and describes the students of his teacher, הלל הזקן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ranks הלל's students by spiritual level. The top level is compared to משה and the next to יהושע. The surprise is the last line: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, the giant we just read about, is called the 'smallest' of the group. This sets up the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught: the opening formula for a ברייתא
Hillel the Elder, the great leader of the generation before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
The smallest (or youngest) of them all

steps.confusionAlert: 'קטן שבכולן' does not mean רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was weak. He was the lowest only compared to this amazing group, and many explain it to mean the youngest.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוֹנִים תַּלְמִידִים הָיוּ לוֹ לְהִלֵּל הַזָּקֵן.
phrases.english: Hillel the Elder had eighty students.
Thirty of them were worthy
that the Divine Presence should rest upon them as on Moses our teacher,
and thirty of them were worthy

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁתַּעֲמוֹד לָהֶם חַמָּה כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן.
phrases.english: that the sun should stand still for them as for Joshua bin Nun.
Twenty were in between.
The greatest of them all was Yonatan ben Uzziel,
phrases.notes: Known for the Aramaic translation (תרגום) of the Prophets.

phrases.aramaic: קָטָן שֶׁבְּכוּלָּן — רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי.
phrases.english: the smallest of them all was Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁמוֹנִים תַּלְמִידִים הָיוּ לוֹ לְהִלֵּל הַזָּקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves back one more generation, from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי to his teacher הלל הזקן and his students.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל's eighty students came in three levels. The greatest was יונתן בן עוזיאל and the smallest was רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

steps.title: Everything רבן יוחנן בן זכאי mastered
steps.stepSummary: A long list of every type of Torah knowledge, from plain verses to hidden wisdom, that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי never neglected.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי that he did not leave out any of these: מקרא, משנה, גמרא, הלכות and אגדות; the fine details of the Torah and the fine details of the סופרים; קל וחומר and גזירה שוה; calendar calculations and גימטריא; the talk of the ministering angels, of demons, and of palm trees; parables of launderers and parables of foxes; a great matter and a small matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how great the 'smallest' student was by listing everything he studied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list covers simple text study, deep legal reasoning, science such as the calendar, hidden wisdom, and folk parables. The point is that nothing was missing from his learning. The list ends with 'a great matter and a small matter', which the next step will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not leave out or neglect
The fine details of rabbinic law
Learning a law by comparing similar words in two places
Calculations of the seasons and the calendar
Fox parables, short stories used to teach lessons

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: They said about Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
that he did not neglect Bible and Mishnah,
Gemara, halachot and aggadot;
fine details of the Torah and fine details of the scribes;
a fortiori arguments and verbal analogies;
calendar seasons and numerology;
the talk of the ministering angels,
the talk of demons and the talk of palm trees;
parables of launderers, parables of foxes;
a great matter and a small matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how great the 'smallest' student from Step 8 was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי mastered every area of Torah wisdom without exception.

steps.title: Explaining the 'great matter' and the 'small matter'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the 'great matter' is מעשה מרכבה and the 'small matter' is the debates of אביי and רבא. It ties his learning to a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A 'great matter' means מעשה מרכבה, the hidden secrets of the Divine Chariot. A 'small matter' means the debates of אביי and רבא. He learned all of this to fulfill the פסוק: 'That I may cause those who love Me to inherit substance, and I will fill their treasuries' (משלי ח:כא).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last two items on the list and then gives a פסוק that his wide learning fulfilled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the debates of אביי and רבא 'small' only means they are smaller than the deepest secrets of creation. It is not an insult to halachic learning. The פסוק describes Torah as treasure that fills the 'treasuries' of those who love ה׳, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was full of it.

keyTerms.meaning: The hidden secrets of the Divine Chariot (from יחזקאל)
The debates and reasoning of אביי and רבא
To fulfill what is said in the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רבא lived hundreds of years after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. It means he already knew the kinds of questions they would later discuss, not that he heard them speak.

phrases.english: A great matter means the Design of the Divine Chariot.
A small matter means the debates of Abaye and Rava.
This was to fulfill what is said:
"That I may cause those who love Me to inherit substance,
and I will fill their treasuries."

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר גָּדוֹל — מַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the last two items of the list in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'great matter' is מעשה מרכבה and the 'small matter' is the debates of אביי and רבא. This fulfills the פסוק about filling the treasuries of those who love ה׳.

steps.title: If the smallest was like this, how much more the greatest
steps.stepSummary: Using a קל וחומר, the גמרא concludes that יונתן בן עוזיאל was even greater. It then tells that birds flying over him while he learned were burned up.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the smallest of them was like this, then the greatest of them was certainly even more so. They said about יונתן בן עוזיאל that when he sat and learned Torah, any bird that flew over him was immediately burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the smallest student to measure the greatest, then gives one amazing story about יונתן בן עוזיאל to show his level. This wraps up the praise of הלל's students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is simple: if the lowest student mastered everything, the top student must have been higher still. The story describes the holiness in his Torah learning as so strong that it burned a bird flying above him. This closes the circle that began in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: How much more so: the language of a קל וחומר

steps.whatToRemember: The chain of praise goes רבי אליעזר → his teacher רבן יוחנן בן זכאי → their teacher הלל and his students. Each level is greater than the last, ending with יונתן בן עוזיאל.

phrases.english: And since the smallest of them all was like this,

phrases.aramaic: גָּדוֹל שֶׁבְּכוּלָּן עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.
phrases.english: the greatest of them all was certainly even more so.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל יוֹנָתָן בֶּן עוּזִּיאֵל,
phrases.english: They said about Yonatan ben Uzziel
that when he sat and learned Torah,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עוֹף שֶׁפּוֹרֵחַ עָלָיו מִיָּד נִשְׂרָף.
phrases.english: any bird that flew over him was immediately burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁקָּטָן שֶׁבְּכוּלָּן כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies a קל וחומר from the smallest student (Steps 9-10) to the greatest (named in Step 8).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: יונתן בן עוזיאל was even greater than רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. His Torah learning was so holy that it burned birds flying above him.

steps.title: New משנה: head and most of the body in the סוכה, table in the house
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. A person sits with his head and most of his body in the סוכה but his table is in the house. בית שמאי say this is invalid and בית הלל say it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone whose head and most of his body were in the סוכה, and his table was inside the house: בית שמאי say it is invalid, and בית הלל say it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The אגדה is over and a brand-new משנה begins. It presents a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל about how a person must sit in the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the person's head and most of his body are inside the סוכה. The only question is the table left in the house. בית שמאי treat that as not properly sitting in the סוכה. בית הלל say head and most of the body is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה': marks the start of a new משנה
His head and most of his body

steps.whyThisMatters: The concern of בית שמאי is that a person sitting near a table in the house may get pulled inside after it.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One whose head and most of his body were in the sukkah
and his table was inside the house:
Beit Shammai deem it invalid,
and Beit Hillel deem it valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיָה רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ בַּסּוּכָּה וְשׁוּלְחָנוֹ בְּתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A completely new topic: the next משנה, after the אגדה ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי say sitting with the table in the house is invalid. בית הלל say it is valid as long as the head and most of the body are in the סוכה.

steps.title: בית הלל's proof from the visit to רבי יוחנן בן החורנית
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל point to a story. The elders of both schools visited רבי יוחנן בן החורנית, found him sitting this way, and said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: Didn't it happen that the elders of בית שמאי and the elders of בית הלל went to visit רבי יוחנן בן החורנית? They found him sitting with his head and most of his body in the סוכה and his table in the house, and they said nothing to him.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל try to prove their view from a real event. Even the elders of בית שמאי saw this and did not object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is based on silence. If the elders of בית שמאי really thought this was invalid, they would have spoken up. Since they said nothing, בית הלל argue, even בית שמאי must accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't it happen like this? An event brought as proof
And they said nothing to him

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
Wasn't there such an incident

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָלְכוּ זִקְנֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְזִקְנֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: where the elders of Beit Shammai and the elders of Beit Hillel went

phrases.aramaic: לְבַקֵּר אֶת רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן הַחוֹרָנִית,
phrases.english: to visit Rabbi Yochanan ben HaChoranit,
and they found him sitting

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ בַּסּוּכָּה וְשׁוּלְחָנוֹ בְּתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: with his head and most of his body in the sukkah and his table in the house,
and they said nothing to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי: לֹא כָּךְ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בית הלל support their ruling from Step 12 with a story.
steps.raayaObject: בית הלל's ruling that head and most of the body in the סוכה is valid even with the table in the house.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The elders of בית שמאי saw רבי יוחנן בן החורנית sitting this way and did not object.

steps.title: בית שמאי reject the proof: they did object
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say the story is no proof. The elders did speak up and told him that, sitting like this, he had never fulfilled the מצוה of סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: Is that a proof?! They did speak to him. They said: If this is how you have been acting, you have never fulfilled the מצוה of סוכה in your life.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי knock down בית הלל's proof. They say the story actually went differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof of בית הלל depended on the elders staying silent. בית שמאי deny the silence and say the elders strongly criticized him. Once the facts are disputed, the story cannot prove anything for בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there proof from there?! A rejection of a proof

steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי are not saying the elders of בית הלל spoke. 'אף הם' means 'they too' spoke up. בית שמאי claim the elders of בית שמאי did object, so the silence never happened.
steps.whatToRemember: The story's facts are disputed: בית הלל say the elders were silent, and בית שמאי say they objected. The basic מחלוקת of the משנה stays in place.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:
Is there proof from there?!
They too said to him:
If you were accustomed to act this way,
you have never fulfilled the מצוה of sukkah in your life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the proof brought in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the story. It does not settle the מחלוקת itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof relied on the elders being silent. בית שמאי say they were not silent and openly objected.

steps.title: New משנה: who is exempt from סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are exempt from סוכה, but a קטן who no longer needs his mother is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are exempt from the סוכה. A קטן who no longer needs his mother is obligated in סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה states a basic rule about who must sit in the סוכה. Three groups are exempt, but an older child is obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule exempts all minors. The משנה then adds one limit: a child who is old enough not to need his mother all the time is obligated. That obligation is from the Rabbis, as חינוך (training him in מצוות).

keyTerms.meaning: Non-Jewish slaves owned by Jews, who keep some of the מצוות
Minors, children under bar מצוה age
Who does not need his mother. Roughly age 5 or 6, when he no longer calls for her as soon as he wakes up.

steps.confusionAlert: The child who does not need his mother is not obligated by the תורה. He is a minor, and the obligation is the Rabbis' rule of חינוך (training).

phrases.english: Women, slaves, and minors
are exempt from the sukkah.
A minor who does not need his mother
is obligated in sukkah.
phrases.notes: This is a Rabbinic obligation, as training (חינוך).

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים פְּטוּרִין מִן הַסּוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not related to the debate between בית שמאי and בית הלל about the table.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are exempt from סוכה. A קטן who no longer needs his mother is obligated.

steps.title: The story of שמאי הזקן and the newborn
steps.stepSummary: When שמאי הזקן's daughter-in-law gave birth, he removed the plaster from the roof and made סכך over the bed for the baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident where the daughter-in-law of שמאי הזקן gave birth. He broke away the plaster of the roof and covered the area over the bed with סכך for the sake of the baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story about שמאי הזקן. He was so strict that he gave even a newborn baby a סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the plaster left only the roof beams, which then counted as סכך over the baby's bed. This seems to go against the rule just stated, that minors are exempt. It shows that שמאי held a stricter view about children.

keyTerms.meaning: Shammai the Elder, the founder of בית שמאי
He broke away the layer of plaster on the roof

steps.confusionAlert: This story does not prove the rule just stated. It shows שמאי's own stricter view, which differs from the rule that minors are exempt.

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה וְיָלְדָה כַּלָּתוֹ שֶׁל שַׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן,
phrases.english: There was an incident where the daughter-in-law of Shammai the Elder gave birth,
and he broke away the roof plaster

phrases.aramaic: וְסִיכֵּךְ עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּטָּה בִּשְׁבִיל קָטָן.
phrases.english: and covered with sechach over the bed for the sake of the baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה וְיָלְדָה כַּלָּתוֹ שֶׁל שַׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story to the משנה's rule. The story shows a stricter practice regarding minors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמאי was strict and made a סוכה even for a newborn.

steps.title: What is the source for the exemptions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that these groups are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a standard question asking for the source of the משנה's ruling. It is setting up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about where the rule comes from in the תורה, not about whether the rule is true. The answer in the next step deals mainly with women and minors.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? A standard request for a source.

phrases.english: Gemara: From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's rule in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for exempting women and minors from סוכה.

steps.title: A ברייתא learns it from the word 'the homeborn'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the word הָאֶזְרָח excludes women, and the word כָּל includes minors.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'Homeborn' means any homeborn person. 'The homeborn' comes to exclude the women. 'All' comes to include the minors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads each word of the פסוק "כל האזרח בישראל ישבו בסכת" closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אזרח alone would include everyone. The extra ה ("the") narrows it so that women are left out. The extra word כל widens it again to include children who are old enough, which matches the משנה's older קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. This introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
'Homeborn' would mean any homeborn person,
'The homeborn' comes to exclude the women,
'All' comes to include the minors.
phrases.notes: This refers to minors who are able to perform the מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ה in הָאֶזְרָח excludes women, and the word כל includes minors.

steps.title: A contradiction from יום כפור
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא uses הָאֶזְרָח to include women in fasting on יום כפור. That implies the word אזרח alone means only men.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'The homeborn' is to exclude women. Is that to say that 'homeborn' alone means both women and men? But it was taught: 'The homeborn' comes to include homeborn women, who are obligated in affliction. Apparently, 'homeborn' alone means only men!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with a second ברייתא that reads the same word the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ברייתא assumes that אזרח alone includes women, so the ה must narrow it to men. The יום כפור ברייתא assumes that אזרח alone means men, so the ה must widen it to include women. The two readings clash.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said. The גמרא quotes the earlier teaching in order to analyze it.
But was it not taught? This introduces a contradicting ברייתא.
Affliction, the fasting of יום כפור

phrases.english: The Master said: 'The homeborn' is to exclude the women.
Is that to say that 'homeborn' alone
means both women and men?
But was it not taught: 'The homeborn'
comes to include the homeborn women,
who are obligated in affliction (fasting on Yom Kippur).
Apparently, 'homeborn' alone means only men!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: ״הָאֶזְרָח״ — לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַנָּשִׁים. לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in the ברייתא of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that הָאֶזְרָח excludes women
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות read the same extra ה in opposite directions, one excluding women and one including them. So what does the plain word אזרח actually mean?

steps.title: רבה: They are traditions merely hinted in the verses
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that both rules are הלכות from tradition, and the Rabbis only attached them to the פסוקים as a support.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: They are הלכות (traditions), and the Rabbis supported them on the פסוקים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה resolves the contradiction by saying the פסוקים are not the real source of either rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the laws come from tradition (הלכה למשה מסיני), the readings of the פסוק are only memory aids (אסמכתא). That means they do not have to be consistent with each other, so the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: A law received by tradition (הלכה למשה מסיני)
They leaned them on, attaching the rule to a פסוק as a support (אסמכתא)

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying the laws are made up. He is saying the laws are real and come from tradition. Only the link to the פסוק is a support.

phrases.english: Rabba said: They are halachot (traditions)
and the Rabbis supported them on the verses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: הִלְכְתָא נִינְהוּ וְאַסְמְכִינְהוּ רַבָּנַן אַקְּרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the source: the readings are only אסמכתא, so they do not need to be consistent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The readings of the פסוק are true derivations, so they must be consistent with each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rules come from tradition, and the פסוקים are only a support.

steps.title: Which one is from the verse and which from tradition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the two rules is truly learned from the פסוק and which is a tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which is the פסוק and which is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses רבה to say which of the two rules is a true reading of the פסוק and which is only a tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'they are traditions' does not tell us how the word אזרח really reads. At least one reading should be the true meaning of the פסוק, so the גמרא wants to know which one.

phrases.english: Which is the verse and which is the halacha?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי קְרָא וְהֵי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the vagueness of רבה's answer in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the two rules is the true reading of the פסוק and which is a tradition?

steps.title: Why is any source needed at all?
steps.stepSummary: סוכה is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, and women are already exempt from all of these. So neither a פסוק nor a הלכה should be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: why do I need a פסוק, and why do I need a הלכה? סוכה is a positive מצוה bound by time, and women are exempt from every positive מצוה bound by time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge: there is no need for any special source to exempt women from סוכה. The answer comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is already a general rule that women are exempt from positive מצוות tied to a specific time. סוכה applies only during the חג, so women should be exempt automatically. A special source for this exemption seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore. This introduces an additional challenge.
A positive מצוה caused by (tied to) time

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next section of the גמרא. It will explain why a special source is still needed, even though the general rule about time-bound מצוות exists.

phrases.english: And furthermore: why do I need a verse,
why do I need a halacha?

phrases.aramaic: הָא סוּכָּה מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא,
phrases.english: Sukkah is a positive מצוה bound by time,
and from every positive מצוה bound by time
women are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: קְרָא לְמָה לִי, הִלְכְתָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the challenge of step 21. It questions whether any source is needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a special source (פסוק or הלכה) to exempt women from סוכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule exempting women from מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא already covers סוכה, so a specific source would be redundant.

steps.title: Fasting on יום כפור Already Has Its Own Source
steps.stepSummary: The challenge continues. Including women in the fast of יום הכפורים also needs no new source, because it is already learned from רב יהודה אמר רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for יום הכפורים, women's obligation is already derived from what רב יהודה said in the name of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in Step 22. Now it attacks the second rule, about women fasting on יום כפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 22 the גמרא said women are exempt from סוכה because it is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא. Here it says women's obligation on יום כפור also comes from somewhere else, namely רב יהודה's teaching. So both rules already have a source, and the earlier discussion about which one is a פסוק and which is a הלכה seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived / it comes out from
From the teaching of רב יהודה

phrases.english: Yom Kippur:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is using shorthand here: it means the rule that women must fast on יום כפור.

phrases.english: is derived from what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav.
phrases.notes: So no special פסוק or הלכה is needed for it.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Continuation of the קשיא in Step 22
steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, מִדְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of Step 22. Step 22 showed that the סוכה rule needs no special source because of the general rule of מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא. This step shows that the יום כפור rule also needs no special source because of רב יהודה's teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The premise behind רבה's answer (Step 20) and the question of Step 21: that a special source, whether a פסוק or a הלכה, is needed for each of the two rules
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both the exemption from סוכה and the obligation to fast on יום כפור already have independent sources, then neither needs a פסוק or a הלכה. The whole question of which is which falls away.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the second half of the same challenge from Step 22. Step 22 handled סוכה. This step handles יום כפור.

steps.title: The Source: "A Man or a Woman"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב יהודה's teaching, which also appears in the school of רבי ישמעאל. It is based on the פסוק "איש או אשה" (במדבר ה:ו).
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and the school of רבי ישמעאל also taught this: The פסוק says, "A man or a woman".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now cites the actual source it just mentioned, so we can see where women's obligation comes from. The explanation of the פסוק continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about sins says "איש או אשה", a man or a woman. רב יהודה uses it to teach that the Torah treats women the same as men for all the punishments in the Torah. Since not fasting on יום כפור carries a punishment (כרת), women are included automatically. The same idea is taught both by רב יהודה in the name of רב and in the school of רבי ישמעאל. That is why women's obligation on יום כפור needs no extra פסוק or הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And the same was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
A man or a woman (במדבר ה:ו)

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is a basic source for the idea that women are included equally with men in the Torah's punishments and prohibitions. The fast of יום כפור is one of these.

phrases.english: For Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
phrases.notes: The גמרא now gives the source it just mentioned.

phrases.english: and the school of Rabbi Yishmael also taught this:
phrases.notes: The same idea is also taught by the תנאים, which backs it up.

phrases.english: The verse says: "A man or a woman",
